settings.eyebrow: A new book by Matthew Estes
settings.lede: Most workplace training teaches people about the work. This book makes the case for learning inside it, with a coach that supports you where you need it and pulls back as you get better.

settings.label: The problem
settings.text: We keep building training on how to ride a horse. The work now runs on cars.
settings.body: AI is changing how work gets done faster than courses can be written. Seat time and completions don't tell you if someone can do the job. This book is about what comes next.

settings.title: The coach
settings.body: Guidance in the flow of real work. You do the task. The coach supports, gives feedback, and helps you reflect on what you did.

settings.title: The throttle
settings.body: Support that fades as you show you can do it. Guide where it's needed. Hand off where it isn't.

settings.title: Four Mondays
settings.body: Four people. Four first days on the job. Stories that show what learning at work could look like next.

settings.title: L&D, changed
settings.body: Not gone. Drastically changed. Practice, community, and the human side of learning move to the center.

settings.quote: You are riding the bike, not learning about bike riding. The training wheels come off as you get better.

settings.label: About the author
settings.bio:
Matthew Estes has spent more than 20 years in organizational learning and leadership development, much of it in healthcare.

He started in sales after school. Like a lot of people in this field, he never knew L&D was a career until he was in it. Today he builds working learning tools, coaches, and simulations instead of slide decks.

settings.label: For organizations
settings.heading: Let's find out together
settings.body: These are concepts based in facts and data. The best way to prove them is in real work. If your organization wants to try the ideas in this book, let's talk.

settings.question: Who is this book for?
settings.answer: L&D teams, managers, and leaders who are watching AI change the work and wondering what that means for how people learn it.

settings.label: Training wheels
settings.heading: You're on the bike from the first minute. The wheels come off as you get better.

settings.title: Leads.
settings.body: Shows each step and why it matters.

settings.title: Guides.
settings.body: Asks what you'd do next, then confirms.

settings.title: Watches.
settings.body: Steps in only when you stall or slip.

settings.title: Lets go.
settings.body: You do it alone, and it checks that you can.

settings.label: Both sides of the evidence
settings.heading: The research cuts both ways. Anyone who shows you only one study is selling something.
settings.closing: The difference is whether the help teaches or only answers. This book is about building the kind that teaches, then gets out of the way.

settings.text: more problems resolved an hour by customer service agents given an AI assistant. The newest agents gained the most.
lower scores once the AI was taken away, for students who had practiced with an AI that handed them answers, compared with students who never had it.

settings.label: How we'll know
settings.heading: Four groups. Same task. Then switch the AI off.
settings.intro: The book borrows a tool from marketing, the A/B test, and names the result that would prove it wrong.
settings.then_text: Everyone does the work with the AI switched off. A month later they do it again, still off.
settings.lose_text: the people who took no course can't do the job without the AI, or can do it on day one but not a month later.
settings.footnote: Appendix A, The Kit, includes a two-group version any learning team can run.
